proposal: The Mandate recommends moving USDA's means-tested food and nutrition programs (SNAP, WIC, school meals and others) to the Department of Health and Human Services so that welfare programs sit in one department. In its description of the ideal USDA, the Food and Nutrition Service would be eliminated, and farm and nutrition legislation would be considered separately.

status_summary: No transfer of nutrition programs to HHS, and no bill or budget proposal for one in 2025 or 2026, was found. On 2026-04-30 USDA announced a reorganization that renames the Food and Nutrition Service the Food and Nutrition Administration, keeps all 16 nutrition programs at USDA, and relocates most staff from the Washington area to program hubs opening by summer 2027; USDA's page and press coverage do not mention HHS. House Democrats (2026-05-08) and 26 senators (2026-05-19) wrote to USDA opposing the plan, citing staff losses of nearly 30 percent, and neither letter mentions HHS. The House-passed 2026 farm bill (H.R. 7567, 224 to 200 on 2026-04-30) and the Senate Agriculture chair's June 2026 discussion draft both keep nutrition as Title IV (the Senate Agriculture Committee approved its bill 12 to 11 on 2026-09-16, with nutrition programs still included), so farm and nutrition programs have not been separated. The readable text of the HHS FY2027 Budget in Brief shows no nutrition-program transfer. A June 2018 White House reorganization plan from the first Trump term had proposed moving SNAP, WIC and some other programs to HHS, but no 2025-2026 equivalent was found.

timeline.event: Agriculture Secretary Rollins issues a department-wide reorganization memo that starts USDA's plan to move about 2,600 of its roughly 4,600 National Capital Region employees to regional hubs (a law-firm alert gives July 24 or July 25, 2025; July 24 is used).

USDA announces the reorganization of its nutrition mission area and notifies Congress: the Food and Nutrition Service becomes the Food and Nutrition Administration, SNAP operations move to Indianapolis, child nutrition to Dallas and WIC and food distribution to Kansas City, with the administrator staying in Washington; neither the USDA page nor Agri-Pulse's report mentions HHS, and USDA says none of the 16 programs is eliminated.
The House passes H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, 224 to 200, with nutrition programs as Title IV extended through September 30, 2031.

Democratic House members led by Reps. Hayes, Craig and Bishop write to Secretary Rollins urging USDA to halt the FNS reorganization, saying FNS has lost nearly 30 percent of its workforce, that the plan appears to skip congressional notification required by Section 716 of the FY2026 appropriations law, and asking 16 questions; the letter does not mention HHS.

Sen. Klobuchar, ranking member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, and 25 other senators write to Deputy Secretary Vaden opposing the FNS reorganization, saying it would close five of seven regional offices and noting that nearly 30 percent of FNS staff left through the Deferred Resignation Program; the letter does not mention HHS.
timeline.source: U.S. Senate (letter, hosted by Sen. Murray)

timeline.event: The Senate Agriculture chairman releases a discussion draft, the Agriculture Act of 2026, which also carries nutrition programs as Title IV.

Under the reorganization plan, all FNA employees are to leave the Northern Virginia headquarters by this date; new hubs are scheduled to open by summer 2027, and the page (updated 2026-09-25) says no programs are eliminated.

The Senate Agriculture Committee approves its farm bill 12 to 11 on party lines; the bill includes nutrition assistance programs including SNAP (a state cost-share for high payment-error rates is among the contested provisions), and the report does not mention any move of nutrition programs to HHS. The existing farm bill extension expires 2026-09-30.

title: Move USDA food and nutrition programs to HHS and eliminate the Food and Nutrition Service
uncertainties: The not_started stage rests on absence of evidence, now from more searches: web searches for bills or proposals to move SNAP, WIC or school meals to HHS (results were the 2018 plan and unrelated 2025 SNAP bills such as H.R. 5822, a USDA funding bill, and the SNAP Study Act, a reporting bill, neither of which moves programs), searches on the FNS reorganization and congressional reaction, and reads of the FNA reorganization page, Agri-Pulse, the Wiley alert, the CRS farm bill report, and two letters. Congress.gov, govtrack and the congress.gov API were blocked or rate limited, so a bill introduced by a member and not covered in news could still have been missed. The HHS FY2027 Budget in Brief text was truncated and its date is not stated in the document (the 2026-04-07 date is approximate); an excerpt of a USDA FY2027 budget summary PDF (date not stated in the document) also showed no transfer. The Rollins memo date appears as July 24 and July 25, 2025 in one alert. Agri-Pulse and Mondaq differ on hub counts and locations; the FNA page is treated as controlling. The choice between not_started and diverged remains a judgment: USDA acted on the same agency but kept the programs and the agency in USDA, which is a different design from the Mandate's.
